findings.on_main: fails the same way (medium: 6 of 20 sampled missing, reply exactly 65,536 bytes)
findings.verdict: existing defect on main, not a regression
findings.root_cause: scripts/gtm-brain-entities/entities.mjs prints --relations with console.log and then calls process.exit(0). The MCP server reads the script through a pipe (server.mjs run, execFile), and the exit drops everything after the first 64 KiB. With stdout to a file the script writes all 179 KiB and nothing is missing; piped into wc it gives 65,536 bytes every time. The lines are unchanged between main and the release. It is the defect lane A fixed for compile --facts (the finish helper in compile.mjs); entities.mjs was not in that lane.
findings.action: marked known_gap in e2e.mjs (PIPE_CUT), byte count in the note. Not fixed: the instruction for a limit that exists on main was to mark it. Fix: write through the compile.mjs finish helper (await the stdout write, then exit), and decide how much of a 180 KiB list a model should get.

findings.on_main: fails the same way (medium: 9 of 10 missing, 65,536 bytes)
findings.verdict: existing defect on main, not a regression
findings.root_cause: The same pipe cut: entities.mjs --customers prints JSON (339 KiB for the medium brain) with console.log, then process.exit(0). The model gets the first 64 KiB of a JSON document, which is also invalid JSON.

findings.on_main: same refusal seen on main messy in every run (the third note of the batch in two runs)
findings.on_release: seen on release messy and medium; in one release messy run it also hit remember.single, remember.batch_script and corrections.supersede
findings.verdict: existing behaviour on main, not a regression and not a lost write; intermittent
findings.root_cause: The notes are written (remember reports all three ids). The query right after is refused: 'query failed: Memory index is busy; retry after the current refresh. database is locked', and the same query 2 s later finds the note. Every index connection takes a coordination lock (lib/memory-index-store.mjs cacheLock, BEGIN IMMEDIATE on work/memory-index-lock.sqlite) and waits 1,000 ms for it. remember ends with lib.rerender, which starts a dashboard render in the background; lib/dashboard-data.mjs and lib/entity-pages.mjs read through the index, so the render holds the lock while it refreshes a 5,000-note index. That the render is the holder is read from the code, not traced. memory-index-store.mjs is identical on main and the release. Refusals per messy run with retries counted: main 4 and 4, release 6 and 4.
findings.action: harness: a read refused with Memory index is busy is retried (the reply says to), and the new check index.read_after_write reports the count as one known gap, so a write check no longer fails at random. Product follow-up: a longer lock wait for reads, or a retry inside the server.

findings.verdict: existing defect on main, not a regression
findings.root_cause: query relations ignores search. entities.mjs line 13 reads options as --name value pairs starting at --relations itself, so the option right after --relations becomes its value and is lost. Checked by hand on both code versions: --relations --entity X returns every relationship (1,598), --relations --entity X --type partner_of returns all 80 partnerships, --relations --type partner_of --entity X returns X's 32 relations of every type. The server always sends --entity first, so over MCP the entity is never applied. The older relation checks passed because the entity is somewhere in the full list; on messy the works_at list is over 64 KiB and the job change falls behind the pipe cut. No suite test runs --relations through the script.
findings.action: new check relations.entity_scope (every line of an entity-scoped read must name the entity), known_gap ENTITY_DROPPED on it and on relations.job_change. Not fixed, for the same reason as the pipe cut. Fix: parse the options after --relations, and a test through the script or the server.

findings.on_release: each failed once, before the harness retried refused reads; pass in the two runs after
findings.verdict: the same refused read after a write as remember.batch_mcp; harness fixed
findings.root_cause: In the release messy run where they failed, batch_mcp showed the Memory index is busy refusal; the reply text of these three reads was not kept in that run, so for them the cause is inferred from the retry fixing them.
findings.action: covered by the retry and index.read_after_write.

findings.root_cause: runChecks killed the server and removed the scratch brain in the same tick; a child of the server was still writing into work/, rmSync threw ENOTEMPTY and the whole run's results were lost (the first main medium run here, and the empty medium-debug.json of the earlier run).
findings.action: e2e.mjs waits for the server to exit and treats cleanup as best effort.

findings.verdict: too slow to generate through lib; measured instead
findings.root_cause: On a quiet machine medium costs about 85 ms per note and the cost does not grow with the number of notes; it grows with the number of entities. A CPU profile of 60 lib.appendMemory calls on the release medium brain (taken at load average 16, so 227 ms per note there): about 85% of the time is the entity registry being read again for every note: readFileSync 39%, parseEntityText 17.5%, parseFrontmatter 12%, lstatSync 7%, readEntityFiles 3%. One lib.readNames costs about half of one appendMemory, so the registry is read about twice per note. Large has 2,470 entities against 1,420: an estimate of 150 ms per note, about two hours for 50,000 notes on a quiet machine. The estimate is not measured.
findings.action: none in code. A registry cache inside lib.withEntityLock would remove most of it.

diagnosis_from_the_earlier_traces.why: The route needs a call to a question tool (question, configuration_question, onboarding_question). Commit 7ed4f4d on main removed those tools: GTM Brain asks through Codex's own box or in plain chat text. codex exec has no box, so the model asked in chat text ('Does Castorama buy in Q4? ...' with three numbered options), which is what the policy says. Reads, no writes and the wording check all passed.

interviewRoute needs exactly one call to the removed question tool, and verify needs one question form in the trace. The final message is one focused question about the broader company pattern, nothing was written. test/define-icp.test.mjs pins the old route with a question call, so the case and that test have to change together; not changed here.

interview() in mentor-shapes.mjs, new in this release, needed a question tool call. The model asked one question in chat text and wrote nothing. Now the route is no writes and the question is checked in the final message. Not rerun.

diagnosis_from_the_earlier_traces.verdict: the case's expectation is wrong for this prompt; one product question is open
diagnosis_from_the_earlier_traces.why: The prompt says 'Anna from finance signed off'. The model looked up Anna (no match) and Castorama (resolved), then asked 'Who is Anna from finance?' with two options and wrote nothing. Rule P3 (a first name alone is never a new person) makes remember hold such a note and ask, and the harness cannot answer a chat question, so the case cannot pass in one turn. The model asked without calling remember first; the remember description says to write first and ask what the result says to ask. Whether the discount should be saved at once without the person link is a product decision. Not changed here.
